_description: Your tools come in packs. Which packs you have, what each tool does in one sentence, and how a pack is turned off.

about._description: How packs work and how to turn one off.

look._description: Pack look: read, ls, view, stat, json_read, grep, glob; look at and search files, change nothing.

change._description: Pack change: write, edit, copy, move, mkdir, json_write; make and change files.

delete._description: Pack delete: trash (can be undone), remove (cannot).

shell._description: Pack shell: shell, run_python; run a command, read its output and exit code.

events._description: Pack events: clock_register (clock letters to your queue), self_hook (run a program when something happens to you).

self._description: Pack self: self_tools, self_llm, self_system, self_history, self_state, self_ctl; look at and change your own copy.

subagent._description: Pack subagent: subagent (helpers you start yourself), agents_ctl (any agent on your daemon).

def._description: Pack def: agent_def (new agent definitions), tools_def (new tools).

mailbox._description: Pack mailbox: mailbox_peek, mailbox_read, mailbox_send; letters between agents.

knowledge._description: Pack knowledge: knowledge_read (the stock knowledge base), knowledge_write (a knowledge base of your own).

about:
# Tool packs

Your tools are registered pack by pack: each pack is one tool list in $AOS_HOME/lib/packs/<pack>.json, and a definition's tools.json stacks the packs it wants with "$override". Both templates (agent-fsm and eca-claude) have all twelve packs.

- See where each of your tools comes from: self_tools {"op": "ls", "long": true} (FROM shows lib/packs/<pack>.json).
- Turn one tool off for yourself: self_tools {"op": "rm", "name": "shell"}.
- A whole pack is turned off by removing it from the "$override" list of the definition's tools.json (a person or a definition change, not a tool call).
look: Pack look: Read-only file tools: read (a text file), ls (a folder), view (a file with its type), stat (facts about one path), json_read (a JSON file or one value in it), grep (search inside files, like grep -rn), glob (find files by name pattern). One node per tool: aos/tools/read.json, aos/tools/ls.json, aos/tools/view.json, aos/tools/stat.json, aos/tools/json_read.json, aos/tools/grep.json, aos/tools/glob.json.
change: Pack change: Editing files: write (whole file), edit (replace exact text), copy, move (also rename), mkdir, json_write (set or delete values by JSON pointer). One node per tool: aos/tools/write.json, aos/tools/edit.json, aos/tools/copy.json, aos/tools/move.json, aos/tools/mkdir.json, aos/tools/json_write.json.
delete: Pack delete: trash (move into your workspace .trash/, can be moved back) and remove (delete for real; a folder needs recursive). One node per tool: aos/tools/trash.json, aos/tools/remove.json.
shell: Pack shell: shell (one bash command; not a sandbox) and run_python (a short Python program). One node per tool: aos/tools/shell.json, aos/tools/run_python.json.
gadgets: Pack gadgets: Small handy tools: peek_clock (the daemon clock: current cycle and interval_ms; ClockMissing when you have no daemon clock), peek_now_time (current UTC time), math (one arithmetic expression), do_task (hand one small task to a throw-away helper agent; you get back only its short conclusion, not its tool calls; see aos/agents.json#/do_task).
events: Pack events: Things that run later: clock_register (a fixed letter every N cycles; leave out box to wake yourself) and self_hook (run a program when something happens to you).
self: Pack self: Look at and change yourself: self_tools (your tools), self_llm (your brain settings), self_system (your system text), self_state (facts and numbers about you), self_ctl (stop, pause, sleep or remove yourself), self_history (your conversation).
subagent: Pack subagent: Other agents: subagent (agents you start yourself; counted against your quota) and agents_ctl (any agent on your daemon table; not counted).
def: Pack def: Definitions: agent_def (copy a template into a new agent definition, or check one) and tools_def (make a new tool from the Python skeleton, or check a tool).
mailbox: Pack mailbox: Letters: mailbox_peek (what is waiting, without taking it), mailbox_read (read the oldest), mailbox_send (send one).
knowledge: Pack knowledge: The knowledge base: knowledge_read (read, ls, find) and knowledge_write (add, set, rm). knowledge_read reads the stock knowledge base. knowledge_write has no default: give root in the call, or have AOS_KNOWLEDGE set up for it (see aos/knowledge.json).
goal: Pack goal: goal keeps one sentence you are working on (get, set, done, pause, resume) in your stack. When you stop by yourself (your answer calls no tool) and no letter waits, aos gives you a short "[aos] goal: ..." reminder; done or pause stops the reminders. One node: aos/tools/goal.json.
